This polymorphism results in substituting

hyperhomocysteinemia.8 
Homocysteine has been identified as a 
risk factor for atherosclerosis in vascular 
disease since the early 1990s, where elevated 
homocysteine ​has been associated with 
hypercoagulable conditions.9 In addition, there 
is an association between vascular disease and
hyperhomocysteinemia, especially in Asian 
populations.10 Consequently, this study aimed 
to analyze the effect of MTHFR A1298C gene 
polymorphism on ACS incidence.
